proof:
The bases are finite by compactness. The lifted hull of the sampled fibers lies in $C$ and contains each fiber at its own base, so the sampled fibers are compatible. Use 1ec728c26c11b368 for continuity of $D$ on each compact fiber and 55a57b1cf55d0c87 for its positive-depth support. The hypotheses also cover the one-fiber case by inserting a dummy real base interval $[-1/4,1/4]$ if $n=0$, whose only sampled site is zero. Ordinary through-point cap volume is jointly continuous in the mark and the unit normal on any fixed positive fiber by dominated convergence off the limiting hyperplane. The compact-sphere minimum is continuous, so $F$ is continuous on each fiber as well. Every cap containing a mark captures at least its own depth in the mark's fiber, including the case of a whole fiber on a vertical boundary. Thus $D\ge F^d$. Both functions vanish on null fibers and on positive-fiber boundaries, while every interior point of a positive fiber has both positive. The finite union of compact fibers gives all maxima. In particular every $P_\lambda$ maximizer is interior to its own positive fiber, including at $\lambda=0$.

Comparing the two chosen sources in each other's objectives gives $\lambda_0\delta\le A\le\lambda_1\delta$, which implies $\delta\ge0$ and gives $A=0$ if $\delta=0$. At a tie of parameters one has $A=\lambda\delta$ directly. Comparing a positive-parameter source with a maximizer of $D$ that has root $F_*$ gives $D(Y)+\lambda F(Y)\ge Q+\lambda F_*$, yielding both individual bounds since $D(Y)\le Q$ and $F(Y)\le F_{\max}$.

The maximum of affine functions with slopes in $[0,F_{\max}]$ is convex and $F_{\max}$-Lipschitz. The maximizing set is compact and the largest slope is attained. The exchange inequality makes it nondecreasing. For parameters decreasing to $\lambda$, compactness gives a subsequential limit of sources attaining the largest slopes. Continuity of $D,F,E$ makes the limit active, so its slope is at most the largest active slope at $\lambda$. Monotonicity gives the reverse inequality, proving right continuity. The right difference quotient is between $F(\lambda)$ and $F(\lambda+h)$ by comparison of the endpoint optimizers, proving the right derivative assertion. At zero the active slopes are the own roots on $\{D=Q\}$.

On each part $(s,t]$ of a partition of $(a,b]$, the exchange inequality bounds the intercept drop between $s[F(t)-F(s)]$ and $t[F(t)-F(s)]$. Summing telescopes the drops. The upper and lower sums differ by at most the mesh times $F(b)-F(a)$, so both converge to the stated Stieltjes integral. The half-open intervals give its endpoint convention. Finally comparison with a source having $(F,D)=(F_{\max},D_{\mathrm{top}})$ yields $D(\lambda)\ge D_{\mathrm{top}}+\lambda[F_{\max}-F(\lambda)]$. This forces $F(\lambda)\to F_{\max}$ and $D(\lambda)\ge D_{\mathrm{top}}$. The nonincreasing intercept has a limit. Along any sequence tending to infinity, a subsequence of actual sources tends to an active source for the limiting maximal slope, so the limiting depth is at most $D_{\mathrm{top}}$ by continuity. Monotone convergence in the work identity at $a=0$ gives the total integral. The bound uses $D_{\mathrm{top}}\ge F_{\max}^d$.
statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $d\ge1$, with positive total summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)$ use closed ambient halfspaces, and let $F(Y)$ be the $d$th root of raw ordinary depth in the actual fiber at $Y$. Put $P_\lambda(Y)=D(Y)+\lambda F(Y)$ and $E(\lambda)=\max_{Y\in S}P_\lambda(Y)$ for $\lambda\ge0$. Put $Q=E(0)$, $F_{\max}=\max_SF$, $F_*=\max_{\{D=Q\}}F$ and $D_{\mathrm{top}}=\max_{\{F=F_{\max}\}}D$. All these maxima are attained and $F_*,Q>0$. At distinct parameters $0\le\lambda_0<\lambda_1$, for any maximizing sources $Y_i$ at $\lambda_i$, write $\delta=F(Y_1)-F(Y_0)$ and $A=D(Y_0)-D(Y_1)$. Then $\delta\ge0$ and $\lambda_0\delta\le A\le\lambda_1\delta$. Every positive-parameter maximizer obeys $F_*\le F(Y)\le F_{\max}$ and $Q-\lambda(F_{\max}-F_*)\le D(Y)\le Q$.

The envelope is convex and $F_{\max}$-Lipschitz. Let $F(\lambda)$ be the largest actual active slope at $\lambda$ and $D(\lambda)=E(\lambda)-\lambda F(\lambda)$ its actual mixed depth. Then $F(\lambda)$ is nondecreasing, right-continuous, equals $E'_+(\lambda)$ and starts at $F_*$. With the right-continuous Lebesgue–Stieltjes convention,
$$
D(a)-D(b)=\int_{(a,b]}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)\quad(0\le a<b),\qquad
\int_{(0,\infty)}\lambda\,dF(\lambda)=Q-D_{\mathrm{top}}\le Q-F_{\max}^d.
$$
The limits at infinity are $F(\lambda)\to F_{\max}$ and $D(\lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{top}}$.
title: Exact work of the actual mixed-plus-own-depth envelope
